newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Dresdner ups London Eurobond business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dresdner ups London Eurobond business.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG on Tuesday announced plans to centralise its Eurobond dealing activities in London, the latest trickle in the steady drain of key activities from Germany's banking capital of Frankfurt.

In a move designed to beef up its role in non-mark business, Germany's second largest commercial bank is buying in a team of experts to steer its Eurobond activities from the U.K. capital, leaving responsibility for domestic issues and government bonds in Frankfurt.

"There will be no physical movement of business from Frankfurt," Leonhard Fischer, joint head of Dresdner's Global Markets Division, told Reuters, confirming a report about the London plans in Germany's Boersen-Zeitung newspaper.
"Dresdner has so far been primarily a mark issuance address," he noted.

Germany's leading banks, vigorously pursuing global strategies, have been building up a larger presence in London in recent years, much to the distress of officials campaigning to have Frankfurt recognised as a leading financial centre.
Dresdner itself last year bought British investment bank Kleinwort Benson for about one billion pounds, an acquisition expected to help fuel a considerable rise in its 1996 profits.
Rival Deutsche Bank AG controls London's Deutsche Morgan Grenfell while Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale earlier this year bought British stockbroker Panmure Gordon.

"This is a perfectly logical fill-in for Dresdner's investment banking business," said Salomon Brothers analyst John Leonard, noting that Kleinwort Benson was mainly focused on equities rather than fixed income.
London was also a logical choice as a focus for Eurobonds, because it has a more vibrant market, Leonard said.
"But I could see in time more business going on in Frankfurt as well," he added.
Dresdner plans to acquire some 16 or 17 Eurobond experts by taking over London-based boutique Luthy Baillie Dowsett & Pethick Ltd (LBDP).
Fischer, who shares responsibility for Dresdner's global bond business, described LBDP as a perfect complement for Kleinwort Benson's international strategy.
Dresdner planned in particular to expand its business with corporate clients and banks and was most interested in LBDP's existing contacts and its credit-spread business.
Fischer also confirmed that Peter Luthy and a partner would take over responsibility for Dresdner's Eurobond business in all major currencies.
The current heads of Dresdner's Eurobond trading, Gerhard Abel and Klaus Roehricht, will report to London from Frankfurt.
In the first leg of its planned expansion, Dresdner will focus on the deutsche mark and sterling sector, moving on to French franc-denominated products and non-European currencies afterwards.
Rumours have also been circulating in Frankfurt that Dresdner also plans to shift its foreign exchange business to the British capital, but this has not been confirmed.
